actions.text: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 36 - 10.
Committee Consideration and Mark-up Session Held
Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.

dimensions.assessment: Affects international local partners, local and national nonprofit organizations, foreign governments, and federal foreign assistance personnel.
dimensions.evidence: local partners, including local and national nonprofit organizations, local and national governments, and local and national private sector entities

dimensions.assessment: Modifies agency procedures, indirect cost caps, and contracting authorities to lower administrative barriers for local entities receiving U.S. aid.
dimensions.evidence: The head of the relevant foreign assistance agency is authorized to increase the de minimis indirect cost rate

dimensions.assessment: Limits local competition awards to caps of $25,000,000 and restricts such awards to no more than 10 percent of amounts appropriated annually to the relevant agency.
dimensions.evidence: Such authority may not be used to make acquisition awards in excess of $25,000,000 and shall not exceed more than 10 percent of the amounts appropriated

dimensions.assessment: Requires comprehensive policy actions, rulemaking, adjustments to federal regulations, and regular reports to Congress regarding local aid delivery.
dimensions.evidence: the head of the relevant foreign assistance agency shall initiate policy actions, including rulemaking if necessary, to institutionalize the actions described in section 4

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent policy authorizations alongside recurring annual progress reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the end of the first fiscal year following the date of the enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter, the head... shall submit... a report

missing_information: The specific identity of the 'relevant foreign assistance agency' is described generally rather than naming a single designated department explicitly in the text definitions beyond pointing to part I of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961.
importance_detail.rationale: The Locally Led Development and Humanitarian Response Act encourages U.S. foreign assistance agencies to shift toward locally led models, adjusts indirect cost rates, authorizes local language application processing, and establishes local competition authorities.
